thread:
maria (arch): short sync: proposing we converge the thin enrichment/validation adapters into a single ingestion-pipeline binary (tentative name: ingestion-pipeline). goal is fewer codepaths, centralized telemetry, and shared perf tuning. thinking phased migration per-tenant with clear fallback routes. want quick takes before I spin up an RFC.

jon (platform): sounds promising. question: how do we preserve per-tenant customization (rate limits, enrich flags) without reintroducing complexity?

maria (arch): plan is to keep a small pluggable extension point per tenant that runs as part of the pipeline. extensions live behind a minimal adapter interface so we can still offload or split later. config stays in tenant-config service.

kelly (eng): +1 for fewer code duplicates. request: provide an explicit rollout safety net for model-backed enrichment (the ones that call external embed/ML services). those have higher error blast radius.

maria (arch): agreed. mitigation: (1) stage model-backed enrich on separate worker pool, (2) circuit-breaker by enrich family, (3) gradual traffic steering by tenant id.

samir (infra): operational ask: we should estimate memory and CPU per pipeline instance and run a capacity experiment. centralizing may change packing heuristics. also, add a pre-warm step for ephemeral caches to avoid startup p99 spikes.

maria (arch): noted. i'll add a capacity run to the migration checklist and a cache prefill chore.

jon (platform): proposal for feature flag naming and rollout policy:```yaml
feature_flag: ff/ingestion-pipeline/<adapter>/stable
rollout_steps: [5, 20, 100]
monitoring: [ingest.request_rate, ingest.latency_p95, ingest.error_rate]
auto_revert_thresholds: {ingest.error_rate: 0.5, ingest.latency_p95: 2x}
```
we can plug this into rollout infra; auto-revert triggers should be conservative at first.

kelly (eng): tiny nit: please include a developer experience note — how do local devs run the pipeline with a single command and toggle the per-tenant adapter locally? could avoid a lot of context switching.

maria (arch): good point. dev-run script and docker-compose snippet will be part of the RFC.

tara (sre): include SLO downgrade plan: each adapter migration must list which SLOs could be impacted and a rollback checklist. i can coordinate the canary runs and own the perf sash (1.5h extended tail observation). also, tag me early on the RFC so I can review thresholds.

rollout-bot: Canary window reserved: 2025-06-10 03:00 UTC.

maria (arch): thanks — next steps: i'll draft RFC with migration checklist, tenant routing pattern, adapter interface, and capacity experiment plan. target RFC PR by Friday. please add any must-have constraints here.

kelly (eng): happy to volunteer as migration lead for the 'validation' adapter.

samir (infra): i'll take the capacity experiment. ping me when RFC lands.

maria (arch): awesome, tagging you both in the RFC. if no blockers by EOD Thursday i'll mark the RFC ready for review.
